content.study:
Introduction
Jurisdiction in CPC is three questions. One: can a civil court hear this at all (s. 9). Two: which court, by subject, territory and pecuniary limits (ss. 6, 15–20). Three: what happens if the wrong court is chosen (s. 21, s. 21A).

Essentials
1. Subject-matter — civil nature, not barred.
2. Territorial — property (ss. 16–17), person or residual cause (ss. 19–20).
3. Pecuniary — s. 6 and s. 15 (lowest grade competent court).
4. Objection to place of suing must be taken at the earliest opportunity and only if there was a consequent failure of justice (s. 21).

Illustration
Contract made in Pune, broken in Nashik, defendant lives in Nagpur. Residual suit — s. 20 lets the plaintiff choose any of those courts.

Fail-illustration
Title to land in Nashik filed in Nagpur only because the defendant lives there. s. 16 governs. s. 20 does not.

Authority
Dhulabhai AIR 1969 SC 78 — exclusion of jurisdiction is strict.
ABC Laminart AIR 1989 SC 1239 — part of cause of action.
Pathumma AIR 1981 SC 1683 — s. 21 timing.

Close with ss. 9, 15–21 CPC, 1908.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain jurisdiction under the CPC.
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Introduction. Jurisdiction is competence.

Heads. Subject-matter (s. 9), territorial (ss. 16–20), pecuniary (ss. 6, 15).

s. 21. Place-of-suing objection is timely and needs failure of justice.

Illustration and ABC Laminart.

Conclusion. Cite ss. 9 and 15–21 CPC, 1908.

questionsAndAnswers.question: A title suit is filed in the defendant’s city. Advise.
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Issue. Is the court competent?

Rule. Land → s. 16. Residual → s. 20. Objection → s. 21.

Application. Title is not a s. 20 suit. Return the plaint under Order VII r. 10 or reject if hopeless.

Conclusion. File in the court where the land lies.
